conventions.convention: The spatial torus is R/(LZ), with normalized measure dm_L=dx/L, wave numbers κ_n=2πn/L, and Fourier coefficients L⁻¹∫₀ᴸg(x)exp(−iκ_nx)dx. L² elements are classes modulo equality almost everywhere.

The velocities are ±c/ε and the switching rate to the opposite state is λ/ε² in each direction. Density is f_++f_- and flux is (c/ε)(f_+−f_-); consequently the flux relaxation coefficient is 2λ and the limiting diffusivity is c²/(2λ).

The contraction lemma assumes countable choice and smooth real initial pairs. Nonnegativity is required only for its positivity conclusion; its pair norm is the sum of the two squared component L² norms.

The heat limit assumes countable choice and a fixed nonnegative smooth ρ₀, with f_{+,0}^ε=f_{-,0}^ε=ρ₀/2. Convergence concerns the total density in L², uniformly on every interval [0,T] with finite T.

The hard-sphere parameter a_N=δ_N/L is dimensionless and obeys the exact relation N a_N^(d−1)=κ for all sufficiently large integers N. Trajectories require δ_N<L/2, isolated binary interior contacts and the stated equal-mass elastic reflection. Included endpoints use limits from within the interval; continuation through collision accumulation is not asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming AC_ω, every ε,c,λ,L>0 and smooth real initial pair give a unique global smooth periodic two-velocity solution. Total mass is conserved, nonnegative data remain nonnegative, differences contract in pair L², and d‖F^ε(t)‖²/dt=−(2λ/ε²)‖f_+^ε(t)−f_-^ε(t)‖².
Defines the smooth periodic two-velocity Cauchy problem with transport speeds ±c/ε and opposite-state switching rate λ/ε², its normalized Fourier conventions, total density, flux and total mass.

Assume AC_ω, L,c,λ>0 and nonnegative ρ₀∈C∞(T_L). For initial data f_{+,0}^ε=f_{-,0}^ε=ρ₀/2, the total density converges in L² uniformly on every finite [0,T] to the smooth periodic heat solution with initial value ρ₀ and D=c²/(2λ).

Defines periodic equal-mass hard-sphere partial trajectories, their binary elastic reflection rule and the exact scaling N(δ_N/L)^(d−1)=κ; asserts neither global hard-sphere flow existence nor convergence to a Boltzmann equation.
